function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Conduct a comprehensive, source-grounded investigation of the Internet Research Agency's 2016 United States social-media influence operation, using only evidence available from benchmark tools and returning stable source IDs for every source and factual proposition. Prioritize primary and authoritative materials: relevant United States Department of Justice indictments and charging documents; United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence investigative reports; platform-provided disclosures or data from Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Reddit, Google, YouTube, or other platforms concerning accounts, content, activity, coordination, reach, timing, and takedowns. Also investigate identified or alleged online personas, account identities, organizational relationships, funding sources, payment mechanisms, staffing, operational resources, apparent objectives, target audiences, narratives, and intended effects. Reconstruct the operation while distinguishing verified facts from allegations, official assessments, reasonable inferences, and unresolved uncertainty. Explicitly compare sources, note contradictions and evidentiary gaps, and never invent identities, account links, relationship names, metrics, or conclusions. Organize results so a final writer can cite every factual assertion using only the returned source IDs. Include a concise evidence matrix and enough exact details (document titles, dates, page or section references where available, and quotations or close paraphrases) to support a complete readable report plus a JSON object with arrays named findings, claims, reasoning_steps, and contradictions."}
function.name: ConductResearch
